papers.summary_en: Abstract: Distributed artificial intelligence training, disaggregated retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) inference, and high-frequency cloud-native microservices place unprecedented bandwidth and tail-latency demands on Kubernetes cluster networking. Conventional Kubernetes Container Network Interfaces (CNIs) and sidecar-based service meshes rely on chained `iptables` netfilter rules and per-pod user-space Envoy proxies that traverse the Linux kernel TCP/IP stack up to six times for a single pod-to-pod RPC.
